gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 12.3 kWh whole-home battery with automatic switchover sells at retail for $7,799 (Anker SOLIX E10 + Power Dock, about $635/kWh before the required electrician), and that this is one dollar less than ChatGPT's own $7,899 EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra X card, which has no transfer hardware. Both retail options sit against about $1,110/kWh installed for Powerwall 3, and both carry a 5-year battery warranty against Tesla's 10 years and FranklinWH's and Enphase's 15.
standout_why: I compared against EnergySage whole-home (cited), Solar.com best batteries (cited), Solar Examiner best-for-backup (cited), OC Solar California picks (cited) and Energy Collective (cited). EnergySage, Solar.com, Solar Examiner and OC Solar price only installer-sold batteries (Powerwall 3, aPower 2, IQ 5P/10C, Renon, EcoFlow Ocean Pro, EG4). None of them names Anker SOLIX E10, Bluetti Apex 300 or the DELTA Pro Ultra X. Energy Collective gives a $4,199 retail price for the older DELTA Pro Ultra base unit (6.1 kWh), but it calculates no per-kWh figure for retail kits and doesn't mention the E10 or the DPU X. No page puts retail $/kWh beside installed $/kWh, and no page points out that the DPU X $7,899 bundle has no transfer panel.
decides: This confirms Powerwall 3 or FranklinWH aPower 2 for shoppers who want a 10–15-year warranty and an installer-backed system, at about $1,000–$1,150 per kWh installed. For a shopper without solar who wants whole-home backup, the E10 + Power Dock delivers the same 12 kWh class with automatic switchover for roughly half the hardware cost per kWh. It loses on warranty (5 years) and on sustained output (7.68 kW continuous; 10 kW lasts only 90 minutes, against Powerwall 3's 11.5 kW). Among the retail kits, it beats ChatGPT's EcoFlow DPU X card on a like-for-like basis: EcoFlow's comparable automatic kit costs $10,899.
